qualityFindings.finding: The address tables visibly document PFOA and PFOS detections and drinking-water-criteria exceedance markings at selected anonymized study addresses.
qualityFindings.impact: They strengthen receptor-result and AOI context and can be cited for the values shown in the official report.

qualityFindings.finding: The report expressly states that the comparability sampling was not intended as a PFAS source investigation.
qualityFindings.impact: The tables and heat map cannot be used by themselves to prove a source-to-Plett migration pathway or to exclude alternative sources.

qualityFindings.finding: None of the seven images contains an executed Plett Road resolution, a final leachate receiving record, or the hydrogeologic and synchronized source/receptor package requested by the evidence queue.
qualityFindings.impact: The unsigned-resolution, exact-final-delivery-date and proven-migration-pathway limitations remain open.

queueResolution.reason: The supplied images document receptor detections and AOI response context, but they are excerpts or annotations of two complete records already held. They do not execute the proposed Plett Road resolution, identify the exact final Wexford leachate load, or supply a site-specific gradient, transect, synchronized source/receptor round, coordinate/sample-ID table and matching field/QC package.

integrityNotes: All seven PNGs were opened, dimension-checked and SHA-256 hashed.
The six address tables were matched by address heading, table values, printed page number and rendered layout to the complete 29-page MPART comparability report.

The annotated Plett image was matched to the official AECOM Figure 3 base map in the existing seven-page Cadillac PFAS Area Maps record; added shading and callouts are treated as annotations, not agency findings.
No cropped or annotated duplicate was added as a separate source record.
